chunks: How many SPI slaves. The question: How many slaves can there be?
SPI has no limit on the number of slaves. The real limits are practical. The master needs one way to pick each slave, and every added chip loads the shared wires a bit more.
So "how many" depends on how many chip selects you can make and whether the bus still works.
Think of a teacher speaking to a classroom. Everyone hears the same voice, which stands for the shared clock and data wires.
But the teacher points at one student, and only that student answers. Pointing is the chip select. The teacher is limited by how many fingers (pins) are free, not by any rule.
The analogy shows one extra rule: students who were not picked must stay silent, or their answers collide.
Independent chip-selects grow linearly; a decoder grows logarithmically (a 3-to-8 gives 8 slaves for 3 select pins); a daisy chain is flat at four wires.
At sixteen slaves it's 19, 7 and 4 pins respectively.
Chip select (CS): the per-slave wire that picks it. GPIO pin: a general-purpose pin on the microcontroller that software can switch.
Decoder: a chip that turns a binary number on a few wires into one active line out of many.
Daisy chain: slaves connected in a line, each passing data to the next, all sharing one chip select.
Tri-state: an output that can disconnect from the wire, so unselected slaves do not fight on the shared data-return wire, MISO.
The basic setup shares three wires (clock, MOSI, MISO) and gives each slave its own chip select. Eight slaves need 3 plus 8 equals 11 pins. A 3-to-8 decoder chip cuts that.
Three pins choose a number from 0 to 7, and the decoder pulls exactly one of its eight outputs low. That needs 3 plus 3 equals 6 pins, plus an enable wire.
A daisy chain needs just four wires in total. That is the whole idea.
"SPI has no addresses, so the slave count is limited by how many chip-selects I can make and how loaded the bus gets. The simple scheme is one CS per slave, costing 3 plus N pins.
If I'm short on pins I can use a decoder on the CS lines, three GPIOs for eight slaves, or daisy-chain slaves that support it so they share one CS.
The electrical limits are bus loading and making sure unselected slaves tri-state MISO."
